stem.text: Predict before the rule: \(f(x)=2(x-1)^{2/3}+3\) is continuous at \(x=1\). Must \(f'(1)\) exist?

options.label: Not necessarily: the one sided quotients decide.
No: a continuous function has no derivative.

resolution.text: A continuous function may lack a derivative. At 1 the one sided quotients tend to \(\infty\) and \(-\infty\), so \(f'(1)\) does not exist.

problem.text: Let \(f(x)=2(x-1)^{2/3}+3\), the power read as a real cube root. Is \(f\) differentiable at \(x=1\)? Give a reason.

steps.cue: The stem asks about \(x=1\): confirm continuity first.
Verdict with reason: compare the sides.
steps.why: Opposite infinite limits: a cusp. Not differentiable at 1.

answer.text: f is not differentiable at x = 1: the one sided quotients tend to infinity and negative infinity.

sections.text: One sided quotients rest on simplifying a difference quotient: evaluate at the shifted input, subtract, divide out the common factor.

stem.text: The quotients at 1 tend to \(\infty\) (right) and \(-\infty\) (left). State the verdict and reason.

answer_key.text: Not differentiable: the one sided quotients have opposite infinite limits, a cusp.

stem.text: Let \(f(x)=3(x+2)^{1/5}+1\), the power read as a real fifth root. Is \(f\) differentiable at \(x=-2\)? Give a reason.

answer_key.text: Not differentiable: both one sided quotients grow without bound, a vertical tangent.
